objective: Implement handoff-ready state and cross-platform interaction guidance for HolyAgent 0.3.4.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-10): "I want you to keep an agent in charge of doing intents and docs and send the stuff to them, so it keeps up-to-date. I expect my weekly limits to end soon I after the 13th I won't have my claude sub anymore and I'll use other agents. that agent can check out other branches and prs readonly. in fact should this be a root directive? have you been keeping everything up-to-date sufficiently? intents, assignments need to be detailed to continue work elsewhere"

Maintainer decision (2026-11-10, chosen over a new scribe specialist role and over a this-session-only fix): a root directive in every model family's root instructions (claude-5.5, gpt-6, kimi-k3.1, via the requirements tree, the family translations and the coverage table). Under it: (1) in the branch state mode the root pushes holyagent/state after each Assignment close and each merge, and before it ends a turn, not only together with work-branch pushes; (2) the Intent in use carries a status-and-open-items requirement, updated at every merge, at every new blocker and before the final report, listing what merged (PR links), what is open (PRs and their CI state), the next concrete step, non-blocking residuals, and what was never tried against the real services, detailed enough that an agent with no session context continues from it; (3) a holyagent CLI command prints a self-contained handoff summary from the state alone (open Intents with requirements, their Assignments with state, objective and outcome, the recorded branches and PRs, and the open items), for another agent or host to read first.
The handoff reader may be a different host or model (for example Pi with Kimi or GPT), so the summary and the instruction text name no Claude-only tool.

Release 0.3.3 follows the repository's release-branch model: release/0.3.3/integration cut from main after the 0.3.2 release merges, the first PR carries mise run bump:patch as its own commit, only the integration branch opens the PR into main. Target: merged before 2026-11-13.

Testing rules carried: never run pi; never make live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI requests; unit tests and fixtures only. Standing authority: squash-merge reviewed green PRs, including the release PR into main; continue until mergeable or blocked.

Design defaults (2026-11-10, revisitable; settled from the code map): (a) the state push stays an instruction to the root (it runs git push origin holyagent/state), not a runtime network write under the state lock, because hosts may be offline and the CLI makes no network calls today; (b) the status and open items live as one Intent requirement that starts with 'Status and open items (<date>):' and is replaced in place at each update, so the Intent schema does not change; (c) the handoff command is read-only like status, reads only local state (no GitHub calls), so it shows the recorded branches and PRs but not their live merge or CI state, which the status requirement carries; (d) the session-start reminder does not change unless its size budget has room.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-10): "outra coisa: modelos gpt tem muito problema em não colocar hover states ou click states (de forma crossplataforma) onde precisa, ajude com isso" (another thing: GPT models often fail to add hover or click states, cross-platform, where they are needed; help with that). Default (revisitable): the visual-work instructions and the design skills (web, mobile, desktop, TUI) require, for every interactive element, a visible hover state where a pointer can hover, a pressed/active state on click or tap, a visible keyboard focus state and a disabled state where it applies, mapped per platform (touch has no hover, so the pressed feedback carries it; desktop and web need both; terminal UIs mark focus and selection), and Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual exercise and capture each state instead of judging a resting screenshot. The requirement goes in the shared requirements tree for every family, and the gpt-6 family's translation states it most explicitly, as a per-element checklist, following its guide.
